currentContext.expansion: FY26 capex activity centred on the EU-GMP CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) programme launched after a June 2025 EU-GMP audit paused the Company's accreditation: manpower reinforcement, investment in new plant and equipment, and an overhaul of systems/processes were submitted and accepted by the remediation committee and auditors, with an EMA re-audit already completed. Alongside CAPA, the Company continued to invest in new capacity, including completion of a dedicated NIP manufacturing suite for the EU/regulated-market business and expansion of the Nutraceuticals manufacturing suite, funded in part by a ~Rs.350 million preferential equity issue. Gross Block Additions during FY26 totalled Rs.409 Mn, of which Rs.108 Mn was directed towards bioequivalence studies and regulatory submissions supporting the Developed Markets pipeline. On the geographic-footprint side, ZIM is in the process of incorporating a wholly owned subsidiary in Chile (LATAM) for business expansion, established a Scientific Office in the Middle East (UAE) in November 2024, and entered a collaboration with Globalpharma Co. (L.L.C.) and a local UAE partner to commercialise and scale Oral Thin Film products across the GCC region. The Company operates an independent, DSIR-recognised R&D Centre and continues technology-absorption efforts (electrospun nanofiber technology, tissue engineering/wound healing, multi-layer film technology, 2D printing on OTF, and the proprietary Thinoral(R) platform). Energy-conservation capex during the year included replacing old chilled water pipelines (~10% energy savings from improved cooling efficiency), upgrading from a 1500 KVA to a 2500 KVA transformer, and installing a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) plant of 150 KLD capacity generating an average of 100 KL/day of recycled water.

risks.note: A June 2025 EU-GMP audit found deficiencies in manual control and documentation processes, pausing the Company's accreditation; regaining it is described as the foremost FY27 objective and a precondition for European market entry and the full revenue potential of the NIP/OTF portfolio.

Geopolitical instability, policy shifts, sanctions and trade barriers can disrupt global supply chains and raise commodity prices, hampering industrial production; management cites geographic and product diversification as the mitigant.

Regulatory approval processes for product registrations and manufacturing (plant audits, accreditations, commercialisation steps) are extensive; delays can hit financial performance, particularly for New Innovative Products targeted at Developed and Pharmerging markets.
The Indian pharmaceutical sector is highly competitive, with large corporations and SMEs competing aggressively for market share, leading to sustained pricing pressure.
The Company operates under CDSCO oversight and evolving global quality/regulatory standards, requiring ongoing certifications, third-party audits and regulatory consultants to stay compliant.

risks.risk: Cyber security and data protection risk
risks.note: Escalating cyberattack, data-breach and IP-theft risk could cause loss of sensitive customer/partner/shareholder data with financial and reputational harm.
Currency fluctuations, inflation and policy changes affect the cost of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, pressuring profit margins.
Escalating R&D costs place stress on margins, requiring prudent and deliberate capital allocation.

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: ZIM Laboratories is a specialist developer, manufacturer and global distributor of differentiated, technology-driven generic pharmaceutical and nutraceutical products in oral solid dosage forms, built on an export-led, multi-regional business model.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: ZIM Laboratories Limited (founded 1984, operations since 1989) develops, manufactures and globally distributes differentiated generic pharmaceutical and nutraceutical products in oral solid dosage forms, supplying Pre-Formulation Intermediates (PFI) and Finished Formulations (FF) across therapeutic areas including Urology, Gastrointestinal, NSAIDs/Analgesics, Anti-infectives, Cardiovascular, Central Nervous System, and Vitamins & Supplements. It serves institutional and government health schemes domestically and exports to 50+ countries through subsidiaries in the UAE, Australia and the EU and a Scientific Office in the UAE.

growth_optionality.body: 17 NIP/OTF products to scale in 24 months; enzyme product (pancreatin) to capture EU shortage; 6 additional innovative products in pipeline; ROW/pharmerging markets to contribute 20% of NIP/OTF revenue; licensing potential

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management attributes FY26's flat Operating Income to two headwinds — the temporary EU-GMP accreditation pause and geopolitical disruption in the Middle East (Q4) and South Asia (Q1-Q2) — offset by a multi-regional business model with dedicated business heads across five key markets
- Export revenue is described as the backbone of operations, sustained by consistent RoW and Pharmerging demand following expansion of the international team and hiring of a President, International Business
- Domestic business margin contribution is driven by institutional supply and growing NIP/OTF traction under government schemes
- The Indian pharmaceutical industry is described as shifting structurally from a volume-based model to a value-driven innovation leader, with the sector pivoting toward market diversification (Europe, Africa, Latin America) to mitigate US regulatory scrutiny and pricing pressure
- Government fiscal support (Union Budget allocation to the Department of Pharmaceuticals, the Biopharma Shakti scheme, and an API import-substitution push) is cited as an industry tailwind
- 14 NIP filings completed to date across RoW and Pharmerging markets
- Regulatory filings completed overall: 14 NIP filings, 29 OTF filings, 14 FF filings
- Regulatory filings completed in the EU: 8 NIP filings, 3 OTF filings
- 57 dossier filings completed to Ministries of Health across RoW and Pharmerging markets during FY26, with 34 approvals received

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin 11.1% in FY26 (down from 13.5% in FY25); cost drag from compliance spend (INR 311Cr R&D), higher finance cost; gross margin healthy at 56%; margin recovery to upper teens expected post-EU GMP with no new CapEx

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritized regulatory compliance (INR 311Cr R&D), CapEx completion, preferential issue deployment; no debt increase planned; focus on cash flow generation post-EU GMP for deleveraging

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 capex activity centred on the EU-GMP CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) programme launched after a June 2025 EU-GMP audit paused the Company's accreditation: manpower reinforcement, investment in new plant and equipment, and an overhaul of systems/processes were submitted and accepted by the remediation committee and auditors, with an EMA re-audit already completed. Alongside CAPA, the Company continued to invest in new capacity, including completion of a dedicated NIP manufacturing suite for the EU/regulated-market business and expansion of the Nutraceuticals manufacturing suite, funded in part by a ~Rs.350 million preferential equity issue. Gross Block Additions during FY26 totalled Rs.409 Mn, of which Rs.108 Mn was directed towards bioequivalence studies and regulatory submissions supporting the Developed Markets pipeline. On the geographic-footprint side, ZIM is in the process of incorporating a wholly owned subsidiary in Chile (LATAM) for business expansion, established a Scientific Office in the Middle East (UAE) in November 2024, and entered a collaboration with Globalpharma Co. (L.L.C.) and a local UAE partner to commercialise and scale Oral Thin Film products across the GCC region. The Company operates an independent, DSIR-recognised R&D Centre and continues technology-absorption efforts (electrospun nanofiber technology, tissue engineering/wound healing, multi-layer film technology, 2D printing on OTF, and the proprietary Thinoral(R) platform). Energy-conservation capex during the year included replacing old chilled water pipelines (~10% energy savings from improved cooling efficiency), upgrading from a 1500 KVA to a 2500 KVA transformer, and installing a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) plant of 150 KLD capacity generating an average of 100 KL/day of recycled water.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Shareholding] Ownership % (June 2026): Promoter 30.3, Other Public 38.8, Body Corporates 26.2, NRI & Foreign 4.6; "Shareholders : 14.5 K" and "Promoter Holding : Free of any encumbrance".
- [External shock] The deck attributes the sequential revenue decline to external factors: Total Operating Income "down 10.5% QoQ due to war situation in the Mid East and serious logistic challenges; some early signs of improvement".
- [R&D talent - internal inconsistency] The R&D slide shows "91 Post-Graduates", "2 PhDs" and "109 R&D Team Size*", while its own footnote states "Includes 27 people from Regulatory Affairs; Net R&D Team is 82 with 71 Postgraduates and 2 PhDs". Both readings are retained as printed.
- [Margin driver] Management's stated reason for the margin move: "Gross contribution margins remained in line with margins for the year FY26 and the previous quarter" while "Lower EBITDA margins primarily due to increased utility and employee costs".
- [IR] Investor relations is outsourced to Go India Advisors alongside company contact Mr. Zain Daud.
